newsitem.title: USA: Medical Device buys royalty rights.
newsitem.headline: Medical Device buys royalty rights.

text.p: Medical Device Technologies said it bought 100 percent of the royalty rights for its Fluid Alarm System (FAS) and 50 percent of the royalty rights for its Cell Recovery System (CRS) from the original developers.

FAS was cleared for marketing last year by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and Medical Device is studying the saturation of surgical latex gloves to show the need for the FAS to alert healthcare workers against possible passage through gloves of pathogens, such as HIV, Hepatitis B and C and other infections agents.
The Company believes the test results should enhance the acceptance of the FAS for all surgical procedures.

The CRS, which also has FDA marketing clearance, is planned for launch in early 1997. The product allows cells to be non-invasively and cost effectively recovered from the bladder and other organs for diagnosis of medical conditions, such as cancer.
